output.brief: The departures are concentrated in one place: 8 of the 11 associates on the Kestrel matter resigned, against 1 of 13 who were never on it. Every Kestrel associate reports to Dorian Faulk, and he works on no other matter with associates. So the data cannot tell us whether the cause is the workload or his supervision. The survey points to both: unsustainable weekends and late-night, publicly copied corrections. The March emails show Faulk and the group head knew the team was overstretched and kept going. Pay does not explain why 12 of 13 non-Kestrel associates stayed. The firm-wide hours target does not either, because other groups have normal attrition. I am fairly sure the cause is specific to Kestrel and Faulk's team. I am not sure which of the two is responsible. Do not announce the £12k payment or close the review. Commission the roughly £9k confidential interviews, designed to separate workload from supervision. Meanwhile, consider low-cost steps such as adding staff to Kestrel. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition tracking. Kestrel's document-review phase runs to December, so act soon.
